svg.title: For E > 0, ρ(E) = (1 −cos E)/E ≥0, with ρ(0) = 0 and |ρ| ≤1. For 0 ≤E ≤1, the inequality sin(Et) ≥2Et/π gives ρ(E) ≥E/π. Fubini applies since both measures are finite and the integrands are bounded. It expresses D as the spatial Fourier transform of the sum of two positive measures: ρ(E) dμ pushed to spatial momentum, and ρ(E) dν pushed to negative spatial momentum. Moreover, |D(x)| ≤M, and D vanishes outside the radius-R ball. Fix 0 < u ≤1 and a smooth nonnegative spatial bump Bu equal to one on |p| ≤u and supported in |p| ≤2u, with Bu ≤1. Its Fourier transform is bounded in absolute value by the volume of the radius-2u ball, hence by C3u3. Since D is supported in a fixed ball, Fourier inversion and positivity imply Z ρ(E)Bu(pspatial)dμ ≤K(R, M)u3,
